That rule is not one of the §C guards, and "refuted" is not a table verb (REJECT lists "not adopted/rejected/declined"). So the refusal-citing-a-rule clause could count against the record or not apply. "Affirmed" (registry boundary) is also not DECLARE-SCOPE's "declared". CREATE-NORM (binding vocabulary) meets its demonstrated-need guard, because the record says conflating the two models "caused every earlier mis-mapping".
- **R-48**: V4 is AMBIGUOUS. "Also closed by this slice: A-1's one labelled evidence limit" credits the closure to the slice's executed result, which is evidence, rather than to a separate act of the ruling. It can be read as a status changing by evidence alone, or as this ruling recording the closure. The triple label "Approval" was not coded as an APPROVE act. It is a type label, and R-62's annotation (listed under others) corrects it.

The guards line says preparation was "previously authorized (R-51)", but the text then says "R-51 granted permission, R-54 starts the clock", and permission alone never allows execution. Read one way, R-51's grant was authorization; read the other, it was only permission. The record also uses the two words interchangeably for the same grant.
- **R-57**: "Corrected" refers to an approved plan, not the record's own text, so it was coded as not-modelled CORRECT rather than CORRECT-TEXT. V5 is AMBIGUOUS: changing the mechanism sentence of an approved plan may partly reverse that approval, or it may only align the plan with R-44 without reversing any decision. V7 is UNTESTABLE. "R-44 superseded" does use the verb, but it describes another record's act, and under F2 that is not this record's act.

It could also be read as this record's own CORRECT-TEXT act, since it is the same day and the same authority, and no other ruling is named. The recording note says the issuing text placed the motion under "Not Part of Ruling" and the register filed it as a ruling anyway.
